prompt.context_jp: ここに一台の古びたカメラ___ある。
prompt.prompt_jp: ここに一台の古びたカメラ___ある。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this opening narration introducing the camera for the first time.

feedback.correct_en: The camera is being introduced for the first time — brand-new information to the listener. 'が' is used to present newly-introduced existence.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'は' would mark the camera as an already-known topic, but here it's the first mention and the narrator is presenting its existence.

contrast_examples.jp: 昔々、おじいさんがいました。
contrast_examples.en: Long ago, there was an old man. (new introduction)

contrast_examples.jp: そのおじいさんは山へ行きました。
contrast_examples.en: The old man went to the mountain. (now a known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 物語___、その残された一枚から静かに動き出す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 物語___、その残された一枚から静かに動き出す。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'the story' as the overall topic of the narration.

feedback.correct_en: '物語' is set up as the overarching theme of what follows — a classic topic use of は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'が' would present it as new information, but the narrator is framing the story as the known subject of discussion.

prompt.context_jp: 杏の反撃:「汚いの___ あんたたちでしょ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 汚いの___ あんたたちでしょ！
prompt.prompt_en: Anzu throws the bullies' insult back at them. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is contrastive は — 'as for who is dirty, it's YOU guys' — flipping the accusation back. The contrast marker fits the defiant tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'が' here would be an exhaustive-listing identification but loses the retort/contrast nuance against what the boys just said about Iori.

contrast_examples.en: The one who's wrong is you. (contrast with others)

prompt.context_jp: 幼い五十嵐唯織は、放課後の路地___乱暴な少年たちに囲まれていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 放課後の路地___乱暴な少年たちに囲まれていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking where Iori was being surrounded.

feedback.correct_en: The alley is the location where the action (being surrounded) takes place — 'で' marks the setting of an action.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'に' would suggest destination/existence point; 'を' would suggest a path traversed, neither fits 'surrounded by boys in the alley'.

prompt.context_jp: そこへ、通りかかった少女の凛とした声___響いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 通りかかった少女の凛とした声___響いた。
prompt.prompt_en: A new voice suddenly enters the scene. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The girl's voice is a new, previously-unmentioned element bursting into the scene — classic 'が' for new information.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'は' would treat the voice as already-known topic, but it's the first appearance of Anzu in the scene.

contrast_examples.jp: その電話は壊れている。

prompt.context_jp: 杏___一歩も引くことなく、まっすぐ彼らを見据えている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 杏___一歩も引くことなく、まっすぐ彼らを見据えている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Anzu, who's already been introduced.

feedback.correct_en: Anzu has already been introduced; this sentence continues describing what she (as topic) is doing. は fits topic continuation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'が' would reintroduce her as new info, but she's the ongoing topic of this scene.

prompt.context_jp: 杏の言葉:「大切なものくらい 自分で___」
prompt.prompt_jp: 大切なものくらい 自分で___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that completes Anzu's command to young Iori.

feedback.correct_en: '守る' (protect/defend) fits — she's telling him to protect what's precious to him himself.
feedback.incorrect_en: '作る' (make) and '買う' (buy) don't match the context of defending the camera from bullies.

prompt.context_jp: 「実は その子___明日 22年と128日ぶりに会うんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: その子___明日会うんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the person Iori will meet.

feedback.correct_en: The verb '会う' (to meet) takes に to mark the person met.
feedback.incorrect_en: '会う' doesn't take を for the person; で would mark a location.

prompt.context_jp: 「この星___ 肉眼だと見えない星なんですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: この星___ 肉眼だと見えない星なんですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Iori asks about this specific star shown in the photograph. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The star in the photo is now the established topic being asked about ('as for this star...'). は marks the topic of the question.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'が' would focus on identifying which star it is, but Iori is asking a property of a star they're both already looking at.

contrast_examples.en: Is this book interesting? (asking about the known book)

prompt.context_jp: 「頭痛 ___見ないで 病院に行った方がいいですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭痛 ___見ないで 病院に行った方がいいですよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word so the phrase means 'don't take the headache lightly'.

feedback.correct_en: '甘く見る' is a set phrase meaning 'to underestimate/take lightly'. Iori is warning not to dismiss the headache.
feedback.incorrect_en: '重く' and '深く' don't form idiomatic phrases with 見る meaning 'underestimate'.

contrast_examples.jp: 相手を甘く見てはいけない。
事態を重く受け止める。

prompt.context_jp: 「どうして僕には 見えないんでしょうか？ 人の気持ち___」
prompt.prompt_jp: 人の気持ち___。
prompt.prompt_en: Iori laments that he can't see something. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: With potential-form verbs like 見える, the thing seen is marked with が. '人の気持ちが見えない' = 'I can't see others' feelings'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は could work for contrast but the natural pattern with 見える for the perceived object is が.

prompt.context_jp: 広瀬裕乃___、タクシーの後部座席で何度も深呼吸を繰り返していた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 広瀬裕乃___、タクシーの後部座席で何度も深呼吸を繰り返していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Hirose, the subject of this descriptive sentence.

feedback.correct_en: Hirose is being set up as the topic whose morning the narration follows. は establishes her as the theme for the following description.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'が' would make her introduction feel like a sudden event-focus, but the narration is describing what she (as topic) is doing.

contrast_examples.en: She runs every morning. (describing a topic)

prompt.context_jp: そのとき、運転席の男___急に胸を押さえ、顔を歪めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 運転席の男___急に胸を押さえ、顔を歪めた。
prompt.prompt_en: A new character acts suddenly. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The driver is being introduced and the sudden action is new information to the scene — が marks this event-focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the driver sound like a known topic, but his sudden chest-clutching is a startling new event.

prompt.context_jp: 「一刻も早く血管造影ができる病院に ___ お願いします」
prompt.prompt_jp: 一刻も早く血管造影ができる病院に ___ お願いします。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for transporting the patient to a hospital.

feedback.correct_en: '搬送' is the standard term for transporting a patient (usually by ambulance).
feedback.incorrect_en: '配送' is for delivering goods; '転送' is for forwarding messages/mail. Neither fits medical patient transport.

prompt.context_jp: 「1人___ 専門出たばっかのひよっこで もう1人___ 大森院長の隠し子って噂…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 1人___ 専門出たばっかのひよっこで もう1人___ ...
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle contrasting the two newcomers.

feedback.correct_en: Classic contrastive は — comparing one newcomer vs. the other. The 'one is X, the other is Y' pattern uses は for both.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present each as new fact without the comparative framing that the sentence clearly intends.

contrast_examples.jp: 一人は医者で、もう一人は看護師だ。
contrast_examples.en: One is a doctor, the other is a nurse. (contrast)
One (of them) became a doctor. (event focus)

prompt.context_jp: 「お医者様の言うことは絶対 これ技師の___」
prompt.prompt_jp: これ技師の___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word meaning 'iron rule' / inviolable principle.

feedback.correct_en: '鉄則' (iron rule) is the idiomatic phrase for an unbreakable principle. It fits the dramatic tone of 'the doctor's word is law'.
feedback.incorrect_en: '規則' is a mere rule, '法律' is actual law — neither carries the figurative 'iron rule' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: This is the iron rule of sales.

prompt.context_jp: 「私___ お医者さんになるんだ パパみたいにどんな病気も見つけるお医者さん」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ お医者さんになるんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Young Anzu declares her future dream. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: '私' is the topic — 'as for me, I'll become a doctor.' This is a self-introduction of her future, a classic topic use.
feedback.incorrect_en: '私が' would emphasize 'I'm the one (not someone else) who'll become a doctor', an exhaustive-listing nuance that doesn't match her dreamy declaration.

prompt.context_jp: 「病気を見つけるにはね カメラマン___いるんだって」
prompt.prompt_jp: 病気を見つけるには カメラマン___いるんだって。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'you need a cameraman'.

feedback.correct_en: With いる meaning 'need/require', the needed thing takes が — presenting it as newly-required information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'cameraman' a known topic, but Anzu is introducing the surprising fact that a cameraman is needed.

prompt.context_jp: 「何で!? 何であなた___ ここにいるんですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 何であなた___ ここにいるんですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Anzu is shocked to see Iori in the hospital. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Exhaustive-listing/focus が — 'why is it YOU (of all people) that's here?' The focus is on identifying the surprising subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a neutral topic question; が carries the shocked 'why specifically YOU' emphasis.

contrast_examples.jp: 君はどこに住んでるの？

prompt.context_jp: 「私はあなたのことを___」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私はあなたのことを___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the humble form Anzu uses to coldly say 'I don't know you.'

feedback.correct_en: '存じ上げる' is the humble (謙譲語) form of 知る used when referring to not knowing a person — polite but distancing, perfect for her cold rejection.
feedback.incorrect_en: '知りません' would be too casual; 'ご存知' is honorific (used about the other person), grammatically wrong here.

contrast_examples.jp: その方は存じ上げません。

prompt.context_jp: 「ここは命___扱う神聖な場所なんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 命___扱う神聖な場所なんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'life' as the object of 'handle'.

feedback.correct_en: '扱う' (to handle/treat) is a transitive verb taking を to mark its direct object.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark a subject; に would be a target. Neither fits a transitive 'handle' verb.

prompt.context_jp: 「この「ドクターズ･ドクター」は 私の___ですから」
prompt.prompt_jp: この本は 私の___ですから。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'favorite book I always read'.

feedback.correct_en: '愛読書' means a book one loves to read repeatedly — a personal favorite.
feedback.incorrect_en: '参考書' is a reference book, '教科書' is a textbook — neither captures the 'beloved reading material' nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 「病院の質___決まるといっても 過言ではありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 病院の質___決まるといっても 過言ではありません。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'the hospital's quality is determined (by this)'.

feedback.correct_en: In a subordinate clause (「...といっても」), the subject '病院の質' takes が. Subordinate clauses typically use が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は tends to stay in the main clause; here the embedded clause needs が for its own subject.

contrast_examples.en: I heard that he's coming. (subordinate clause)

prompt.context_jp: 「でも 日本___は いまだに 医者といえば臨床医」
prompt.prompt_jp: でも 日本___ いまだに 医者といえば臨床医。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle contrasting Japan with America (just mentioned).

feedback.correct_en: 'では' explicitly contrasts Japan with the previously-mentioned America. The は after で adds contrastive framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'が' would mark subject; 'に' alone doesn't carry contrast. 'では' is the right contrastive location marker here.

contrast_examples.jp: アメリカでは普通だが、日本では珍しい。
contrast_examples.en: Common in America, but rare in Japan.

prompt.context_jp: 「早く___になりたいんです やらせてください！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 早く___になりたいんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'a full-fledged professional'.

feedback.correct_en: '一人前' means a fully-qualified, independent professional — exactly what Hirose aspires to become.
feedback.incorrect_en: '一人分' is 'one person's portion/share'; 'お一人様' is a polite 'one customer' — neither fits 'become a full professional'.

prompt.context_jp: モニターの画像を見て:「脳___とけてる！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 脳___とけてる！
prompt.prompt_en: Hirose exclaims at the strange MRI image. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is an exclamation about a newly-noticed, shocking state. が marks the subject of a sudden observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would sound like a calm topic statement; the moment is a startled discovery, which demands が.

prompt.context_jp: 「金属___あると磁場が乱れて 信号を正しく読み取れず...」
prompt.prompt_jp: 金属___あると磁場___乱れて 信号を正しく読み取れない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle appearing twice in this conditional explanation.

feedback.correct_en: In a conditional (〜と) clause, the subject takes が. '金属があると' and '磁場が乱れて' both describe cause-effect events needing が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn these into topic statements; in a conditional 'if/when X happens' structure, が marks the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降ると、道が濡れる。
contrast_examples.en: When it rains, the road gets wet.

prompt.context_jp: 杏が少年たちに立ち向かう場面:「汚いのはあんたたちでしょ！」
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Anzu's defiant retort to the bullies who called Iori 'dirty'?

choices.text: 汚いのはあんたたちでしょ！
汚いのがあんたたちでしょ！
あんたたちは汚いのでしょ！

feedback.correct_en: The cleft structure 「汚いのは〜」puts the predicate 'dirty' as the given (contrastive) topic and identifies 'you guys' as the answer — the natural retort shape.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) 'のが' breaks the contrastive flip; (c) rearranges into a flat statement that loses the sharp throw-back energy of the comeback.

contrast_examples.en: The one who's bad isn't me.

contrast_examples.jp: 間違っているのはあなたです。
contrast_examples.en: The one who's wrong is you.

prompt.context_jp: 杏が放射線技師たちに苛立ちをぶつける場面
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing most naturally captures Anzu's cool but curt professional demand to the technicians?

choices.text: 何とかしてください。それが皆さんの仕事ですから。
何とかしてよ。それあなたたちの仕事じゃん。
何とかしていただけないでしょうか。お仕事ですから。

feedback.correct_en: (a) keeps professional politeness (〜てください / 〜から) while still being firm and curt — fitting her role as a doctor pulling rank on technicians.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is too casual for a workplace confrontation; (c) is overly soft/humble, undercutting her commanding tone.

contrast_examples.jp: これはあなたの仕事ですから、やってください。
contrast_examples.en: This is your job, so please do it. (firm-polite)
Just do it, it's your job. (too casual)
